epilogue_text:
On every rock of the valley the Camunni carved their roses. You found fourteen, one for every place the fog had emptied.
The fifteenth is on the cemetery bench, where Ottavio woke up. It is small, freshly carved, crooked the way a child would carve it. Next to it are two initials, one large and one small: N. and L.
When the fog comes back in November, someone at the town hall swears the radio switches itself on. Two voices, on channel 9. Laughing.
Brescia_Edolo_intro_1: For twelve days grandma Teresa has not answered the phone. The news says the road to Malonno is closed by a landslide. Nobody, though, has seen the landslide.
Brescia_Edolo_intro_2: You drive up anyway, at night, along the Brescia-Edolo road. At the fork the fog turns so thick that the engine dies by itself. In the silence the car radio crackles: "...if anyone can hear me, don’t stay on the road."
clue_Brescia_Edolo: A two-way radio, still on, tuned to channel 9. The voice comes from here: someone in the village is still talking.
Brescia_Edolo_outro_1: "I can see you, you know," the voice says. An old woman, calm. "I’ve got the binoculars on the road. Follow the street lamps to the village sign. And never step out of the light."
Welcome_intro_1: The sign says MALONNO. The windows are dark, but the bar sign is still lit. On the cobbles lies an open newspaper, stuck on the same page for twelve days.
clue_Welcome: The valley newspaper of 2 November: "Thick fog tonight in the upper valley, residents are advised to stay indoors." It was All Souls' night.
Welcome_outro_1: "My name is Nives, I work the town hall switchboard," the radio crackles. "There are only a few of us left. Maybe only me. Your grandmother? That evening she was at the grocery, I saw her go by. Go and look."
Formis_intro_1: In the grocery everything stopped halfway: the slicer halted on a pound of ham, the change still on the counter, the light on above the till. As if people had stepped out for a moment and never come back.
clue_Formis: Grandma Teresa’s shopping list, in her crooked hand: bread, milk, grave candles for All Souls. At the bottom, in pencil: "Gino is taking the pizzas to the Villa."
Formis_outro_1: "Villa Rosa," Nives sighs. "That evening engineer Ottavio had invited half the village. He said he had found something in the cellar. Dinner came from the Pizza King."
Pizza_King_intro_1: The Pizza King’s oven has been cold for days. The tables are still laid, and in the window the papier-mache lion stares at the empty street.
clue_Pizza_King: A receipt from 2 November: fourteen pizzas, delivery to Villa Rosa, 9 pm. On the back, in pen: "Don’t go. The stone must not be touched."
Pizza_King_outro_1: "The stone..." For the first time Nives' voice shakes. "Come to the town hall. The door is open. There is something in the archive you need to see."
Municipio_Abbandonato_intro_1: There is light in the registry office: a green lamp and an old valve radio, switched on. No sign of Nives. Only her voice, from the speaker: "Look in the archive. Year 1966."
clue_Municipio_Abbandonato: A photo from 1966: a little girl in a coat in front of Villa Rosa. On the back: "Lucia Rosa, aged 7. Lost in the All Souls' fog." She was Ottavio’s sister.
Municipio_Abbandonato_outro_1: "Ottavio never stopped looking for her," Nives says. "He read the old papers: the fog takes people away and the stone holds it still. Break the stone, and the fog gives back what it took."
Municipio_Abbandonato_outro_2: "I think he broke it. And instead of giving back, the fog took everyone. If there is a way to set it right, start at the hotel: the man from Milan was staying there."
Albergo_Lobby_intro_1: At the end of October a man from Milan checked into the Alpine Hotel: an antique dealer, people said, come especially for Ottavio. The guest register is still open on the desk, the pen lying across it.
clue_Albergo_Lobby: A fragment of grey-violet stone, pecked with tiny blows: part of a pattern that winds around itself like a flower. Valley sandstone, like the rocks of Sellero.
Albergo_Lobby_outro_1: "It’s the Camunian Rose," Nives says softly. "Our ancestors carved it on the rocks before the Romans came. If one piece is here, the dealer was carrying off others. But stop at the infirmary first. You need to know what the fog does."
Infermeria_Alpina_intro_1: The village infirmary. Two unmade beds, the medicine cabinet open, a flickering neon tube. On the table lies Doctor Bettoni’s notebook, densely written up to the last evening.
clue_Infermeria_Alpina: From the doctor’s notebook: "Three people found in the fog, asleep. They breathe but do not wake. In their sleep they all repeat the same word: rose."
Infermeria_Alpina_outro_1: "They are not dead, do you understand?" Nives' voice cracks. "They are sleeping, somewhere inside the fog. If we put the stone back together, maybe they wake up. Go to the Villa."
Villa_Rosa_intro_1: Villa Rosa stands black against the sky. The gate is open and a window has been smashed from the inside. In the yard there are overturned chairs and fourteen pizza boxes, never opened.
clue_Villa_Rosa: An iron key on a red ribbon. On the tag, in Ottavio’s hand: "Cellar. Forgive me, Lucia."
Villa_Rosa_outro_1: "The cellar," Nives says. "Go down slowly. And if you hear someone calling your name, don’t answer."
Sotterranei_Villa_Rosa_intro_1: At the back of the cellar, behind the wine press, a wall has been knocked down with a sledgehammer. Inside is an empty niche, the size of a gravestone. A thin, cold thread of fog rises from it.
clue_Sotterranei_Villa_Rosa: Ottavio’s chisel, its tip dusty with violet powder. In the dust on the floor, the marks of five pieces dragged away in different directions.
Sotterranei_Villa_Rosa_outro_1: "Five pieces," Nives counts. "You already have one. The others were taken by the people who tried to stop the dealer that night. The firemen, for a start. They all went out, sirens on."
Caserma_Pompieri_intro_1: The volunteer fire station. The beacon is still turning, red on the walls. The board reads: crew out 2 November, 22:40. No return.
clue_Caserma_Pompieri: The second piece of the Rose, wrapped in a fireman’s jacket. The crew chief must have wrenched it from the dealer’s hands before the fog took them.
Caserma_Pompieri_outro_1: "Two," Nives says. "That night Mazzoli from the garage towed the dealer’s van away with the breakdown truck. If there was anything else, it’s still there."
Officina_Abbandonata_intro_1: The Mazzoli garage still smells of oil and iron. On the lift stands a white van with its doors flung open. The back has been emptied in a hurry.
clue_Officina_Abbandonata: The third piece, under a pile of rags, with a shipping label: "Milano Centrale. Fragile." The dealer meant to leave by train.
Officina_Abbandonata_outro_1: "The Sunday heritage train is still at the station," Nives says. "They closed the line that very night. If the rest of the stone left, it didn’t get far."
Stazione_Abbandonata_intro_1: Malonno station. The old steam engine stands on the track with no stoker. Under the canopy lies an open suitcase, clothes scattered among the weeds.
clue_Stazione_Abbandonata: The fourth piece, in the dealer’s suitcase. With it, a one-way ticket to Milan, never stamped.
Stazione_Abbandonata_outro_1: "One missing," Nives says. "The biggest, the heart of the Rose. Ottavio must have kept it. Every year, on All Souls' evening, he went to church to light a candle for Lucia."
Chiesa_Abbandonata_intro_1: The old church is ice cold. On the side altar burn candles that nobody can have lit. On the floor in front, the marks of someone who knelt there for a long time.
clue_Chiesa_Abbandonata: The heart of the Rose, laid on the altar beside a little girl’s shoe. Ottavio came this way. Then he climbed to the cemetery.
Chiesa_Abbandonata_outro_1: "The cemetery, above the village," Nives says. "The stone stood there, in the ossuary, before the Rosa family walled it up in the cellar. Take it home. Dawn is coming."
Cimitero_Montagna_intro_1: The mountain cemetery. The fog is so thick here it feels like walking inside it. In the ossuary an empty niche waits for its stone. And on the bench, someone is asleep.
clue_Cimitero_Montagna: A silver locket with the photo of a little girl: Lucia. Ottavio was holding it, asleep on the bench. He is breathing.
Cimitero_Montagna_outro_1: You set the last piece in place. The carved lines close up one after another, until the Rose is whole again. Down in the valley a bell starts to ring.
Cimitero_Montagna_outro_2: The fog pulls back like a tide. Out of the houses, the streets, the station, people come out dazed, as if they had slept too long. In the square a woman in her Sunday coat calls your name. It’s grandma Teresa.
Cimitero_Montagna_outro_3: Ottavio is the last to wake. He says nothing. He looks at the Rose, then at the locket, and leaves it in the niche beside the stone. "Lucia stayed on the other side," he says. "But now I know she is not alone."
Cimitero_Montagna_outro_4: Nobody finds Nives. At the town hall the valve radio has been dead for years, its wires cut and grey with dust. In the registry, under B, it says: "Bonomi Nives, switchboard operator. Lost in the All Souls' fog, 2 November 1966."
